title: Possession and pointing
vocabFocus: tu, su, nuestro; este, ese, aquel
practiceFocus: Describe your things versus someone else’s, and point to three objects

points.title: More owners, and three distances
points.rule: Day 6 only used mi and mis. Tu and tus mean your. Su and sus mean his, her, or their. Nuestro matches gender and number: nuestro, nuestra, nuestros, nuestras. Mi, tu, and su only match number. Este and esta are near you, ese and esa are near the listener, and aquel and aquella are far from both.

examples.english: Our family is small. Nuestra matches familia.

examples.spanish: Esa camisa es bonita. Aquella casa es de mis vecinos.
examples.english: Esa is near the listener. Aquella is far from both.

grammar.notYet: The long possessive forms used after the noun, like es mío.

phrases.english: His, her, or their house is very big.

phrases.note: Reuses the day 6 fact, now with nuestra.

phrases.english: Those buildings over there are old.
I prefer this one to that one.

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.spanish: Esta es nuestra casa. Es pequeña, pero nos gusta.
lines.english: This is our house. It is small, but we like it.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.spanish: Es muy bonita. ¿Y esa casa de allí, la grande?
lines.english: It is very nice. And that house over there, the big one?

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.spanish: Aquella casa es de mis vecinos. Su jardín es enorme.
lines.english: That house belongs to my neighbours. Their garden is huge.

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.spanish: Sí, este es nuestro jardín. Es pequeño, pero suficiente.
lines.english: Yes, this is our garden. It is small, but enough.

practice.title: Yours, mine, and pointing
practice.instruction: Describe two of your things using mi or mis, then two things that belong to someone else using su, sus, or nuestro. Then point to three objects: one near you, one near the listener, one far away, using este, ese, and aquel.
tips: Match nuestro to the noun’s gender and number, like an -o or -a adjective.
Mi, tu, and su only match number.
